subject: literature
passage: Over the winter, Tomas and his younger brother Luis set out to build a telescope from a secondhand kit, grinding the mirror by hand with abrasive powder and water. The instructions promised a finished mirror after forty hours of work. ______ after sixty hours the glass still showed the faint scratches that the final polish was supposed to remove, and Luis began to ask whether a telescope from a shop would have been simpler. Tomas kept grinding, convinced that one more evening would do it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The second sentence sets an expectation: the instructions "promised a finished mirror after forty hours." The next sentence reports what actually happened: after sixty hours the mirror was still scratched. The transition must signal that reality went against the promise.
explanation.A: Correct. "Yet" signals a contrast between the promise of forty hours and the reality of sixty hours with the mirror still unfinished.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The actual result is not similar to the promised result; it falls short of it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Sixty hours of grinding with scratches remaining is not an example of what the instructions promised.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In addition" would add a point of the same kind, but the scratches after sixty hours go against the promise rather than adding to it. This is tempting because the sentence does add new information.
